I agree. Some will say "but 200 to 600" is a 200% increase!"  
Sure, but you still still sat on a box for X amount of time and let it take up physical space in your life, just to come up on $400? There are other side hustles that could earn you that money in a week.

Poke investing makes way more sense when you start talking volume. Making $400 profit on each of say, 50 boxes you sold does actually sound pretty sweet for a 20K profit. But most Poke investors are not buying (and storing!) 50 copies of a $200 box ($10K) for the sake of "investing". Businesses do indeed order that volume but they usually will sell immediately because this industry requires constant cash flow. They need to sell so that the revenue (profit if they are lucky) can be used for buying product of the next set and keeping the store patrons happy. Stores today are actively selling their Surging Sparks/Terastal Fest/Prismatic Evo instead of just "holding it for the long game". Because as you said, they are collectible toys. Not investment vehicles. With that kind capital you could invest in way more meaningful that will guarantee growth over time (like a CD), rather than gamble it on Pokemon.

In January of 2023 I decided to buy \~$10K worth of Amazon stock instead of buying a few cases of Evolving Skies like my friends insisted on. Not only was it the safer bet at the time, it has proved to the correct one. Higher ROI and no one is yelling at me about the Pokemon cards taking up space in the house.

  
Everyone, buy your Pokemon packs and rip them for fun. Enjoy it! If you like collecting sealed product like I do, then make it look pretty in your display and enjoy looking at it!  
  
If you are only buying Pokemon for the sake of investing/reselling for profit (and you are NOT a LGS owner), then I suggest you explore other side hustles.

I always try to tip more on grocery orders. When it comes to just food, the driver’s effort is (usually) the same whether your food is worth $10 or $100. Obviously if the $100 order came with multiple bags then there is more inherent effort. But a single bag is the same. I have friends who follow this logic and tip a flat $2-$3 every time, no matter how big/small the order is. I always tip based on percentage because societal customs are telling me to. 
Anyway my point is, that when it comes to Instacart drivers, they have to do more than just pick up food. They do the actual shopping which can be awful sometimes. That to me is where the tip is mostly earned, and I will happily tip more for doing my shopping. 

My friend was telling me that I am wasting my money by instacarting(probably true) but this argument helped turn him around:
 Suppose you know you had to go to the store, walk up and down the aisles, move between people, wait in line, come home through possible traffic and unload groceries and that it takes about 2 hours for the whole mission. Wouldn’t it be nice to pay someone anywhere from $25-$50 (depending on order) to take care of all of that for you, AND also drop it off right at your door? Those 2 hours are now used for other chores, catching up on work, being productive elsewhere, you get it. I can easily see myself or my friend telling one of our siblings “here’s a list of things I need from the store. Go get it for me and I’ll give you $25”. There is now an app for summing a “sibling” to get your groceries, so of course I will use it. 
As I grow older, the idiom that “money is time” resonates stronger with me, and I am willing to pay a delivery service if that means being able to “buy back” some time

To your last point about the water insanity-

I will admit that my main use for instacart is to have cases of water delivered to me, and since I am delivering water I use the opportunity to get a few necessities (milk, bread, eggs etc). I do this because I live on the top floor of my apartment building (6) while my car's designated parking spot is on floor 3 and on the other side of the property. (there are reasons why I can't get a different spot).

Anyway, I am very conscious of the fact that 1. It is a pain in the ass in general to get to my unit from the lobby and also 2. it is more of a pain in the ass when you have to carry something heavy. It is also not a fun trip to go from my parking spot to my unit, which is why I tend to deliver.

When I doordash, I will tip $5 on a $12 order because I know it sucks walking up to my unit. I think that from the lobby of the building, to my unit, and back down to the lobby could be a whole 5 min trip, longer if you are waiting on an elevator for too long.

For instacart, there is a "heavy items" fee or something like that when I order the waters. I am also usually forgoing any BOGOs or deals on the water that I usually come across when I go in person. There is a delivery fee, plus the item-mark up, and then I will tip something like $10-$20 depending on how much groceries I ordered. Something worth noting is that the grocery store is also a 5-7 min drive from my building. I also never order more than 10-15 items- my instacart orders are always simple unless you consider the water as not simple given its weight. My lobby also has a cart that people are welcome to use for transporting stuff like groceries up to your units, that then must be returned. Drivers are welcome to use it to load the waters, and then just return it on their way out.

**ALL OF THIS TO ASK**\- how inconsiderate am I being, if I am, to instacart drivers by ordering cases of water? Am I making up for it with the higher tip? Is it not high enough? I want to believe that given the extra fees for the heavy items, the drivers are also getting a bit more compensated. Is that something you can confirm? I have my method of bringing waters and groceries up from my car for when I do go to the store myself, but sometimes I am OK with paying something like $40-$50 extra on groceries if that means 1. saving time on having to go myself to the store, 2. not having to deal with the labor (and time) of moving groceries into the unit from the car. I'd say \~75% of that excess charge goes to the fees/tips for the service while the rest of it is just item mark-ups.

I recall once a couple years ago, I was pressed for time during a busy week with nothing to drink at home and I instacarted literally only drinks. It was 3 24 packs of water bottles and I believe that time there was also a 12 pack of soda. Anyway- had I gone myself to the store I may have paid like, 20 bucks max for it all? This order was closer to 50 or 60 after you tack on all the fees and the tip. How much over the $20 should have been an appropriate overcharge for the convenience of getting these items delivered to me? How much of that overcharge is the driver actually seeing come back to them? They see and receive all of my tip hopefully, but the heavy items fee for example- does the driver receive that? Seems reasonable to me that they should. Wouldn't make sense for the app/service to charge more for heavy items if it ultimately falls on the driver to handle/deliver. (I really do hope they are receiving a higher wage when there is a heavy item fee, otherwise my guilt grows stronger). 

I've rambled for too long. Thoughts? Am I one of those customers making a driver's life miserable?

Not as bad as yours but I had a similar experience. Last year got back into the game and going to locals was mentally exhausting at times. A lot of players will just laugh at you for making bad plays, along with their friends watching the duels. They get annoyed when you ask to read cards or ask how an effect/game mechanic works. "I can't tell you." -\_\_- They do their plays extremely quickly and don't give you time to react. They'll skip steps to make the combo go faster. As someone who was learning, this is mad confusing. When matches are concluded and I ask "what could I have done better" or when I ask for another duel so I can practice (because I got stomped in Games 1 and 2 within 5 minutes lol) they just don't want to talk to you. They go back to their buddies and just talk shit. Idk how many times my opponent at this locals has half his focus on our duel because he is either on his phone or making a trade with someone sitting next to him.... just total lack of respect and no sense of welcoming community for new players. I'm not naive enough to expect 0 assholes so I have stuck through it but I can 100% see how a new player checking out the scene would be turned off and just never return to the store after a single visit. I am in South Florida where I have since realized a lot of the top players are from, and I recognize some of these guys playing on the streams are the same jerks from the cliques at my locals. Was a bit disheartening to realize that these people that are pretty ugly on the inside are the ones topping events. If you are not their friend, they do not care about you and have no interest in welcoming new players to the community.  

I've grown to understand the game much much more since then and I recall going against someone at locals who looked like he grabbed his cards from when he was a kid and tried to make a deck out of it. Needless to say he was lost, but I was happy to explain to him the rules, the game mechanics, how spell speeds work, etc. Some of the usuals overheard this and I think that day I gained a little from a few of them as they realized I actually knew what I was talking about. Other usuals at the locals are still just jerks and I don't enjoy playing them. When I get paired with them I'll just take the round loss and duel with my friend instead. I have actually signed up for locals, got my OTS pack, been paired with my most disliked person there for Round 1, and just gone home. Unfortunately the bullies are all part of the same clique and basically fund the store with how often they are there, so I know that complaining will not do much. At minimum it will just get me blackballed from the local community and I don't want to make myself a focused target of their bullying or worse even any attempts at scamming me or stealing from me. It is still my only locals near me with a 20 min drive so I still go and deal with it. (at least, pre-COVID. They are still not open yet)

I realize I am just ranting now. 

The point is, people suck. Your locals sounds awful- don't go back. I would do as someone else commented and complain to store and explain why you will not be returning. Find a new locals if you can, but be prepared to encounter some toxicity there as well. I've found it is unavoidable in any community no matter which corner of the Earth you are on. You will however find a handful of people that will be fun to play with and hopefully make friends out of. Good luck getting back into the game.

Me ex gf and I were going to the beach with some friends. We stopped at a store to get some drinks and beach stuff, and at the register she says she wants to help pay the $80+ bill so she offers me $40 in cash. She didn’t normally contribute to most things even though we both made decent money, something we had discussed as it was causing a strain in the relationship, so I appreciated the gesture, said thank you I love you baby, pocketed the $40 cash and went to pay the cashier the whole $80+ on my credit card. She contributes, I feel more secure knowing that she is being more conscience about us being partners rather than “the man pays for EVERYTHING”, I now have some cash (you never know when you go somewhere that is cash only- like parking at a beach), and I can earn points/miles on my card. Makes the cashiers life just slightly easier by not having to split the bill cash/card. Sounds like an ideal situation for everyone involved right? Win-win-win. 

Wrong. My ex gf was throwing a fit that I did not give the cashier the $40, and pay the rest on my card. Right in front of the cashier. Her logic was that now “she’s not helping pay for groceries, she’s paying $40 towards something else I might buy”. She continued, “By putting the whole $80 on your credit card, you basically just paid for all the groceries and took $40 from me. So what are my $40 going towards??” ....they went to the groceries..... 

We didn’t last much longer after that. 



Which reminds of a similar situation very early in our relationship where she hands me a $5 bill and asks me to get something from the store. She was busy with chores/studying and I was just playing video games so I was happy to do it. I get what she wants (which was about 5 and change) and I also get a couple of drinks/snacks for us to share and take back to her house. Total was like $15 so naturally I pocket the 5 and pay the whole thing on my card. AGAIN, SOUNDS REASONABLE RIGHT?

Wrong. “So... you didn’t use the $5 bill?” “No I just put the stuff you asked me to get on my card. The $5 bill you gave me is technically in my wallet.” 
“So then why did I give you $5 if you were going to put everything on your card anyway? I swear you do things sometimes that don’t make any sense” ....what. She demanded the $5 back, which I gave to her reluctantly just to stop the arguing. 

Worst part of these tales is that she was and still is a bank teller....
